summary.title: Stop learning frameworks
summary.one_liner: Spend most of your learning time on transferable fundamentals (design patterns, clean code, DDD) rather than on short-lived frameworks, using the Lindy effect as the reasoning.
keywords: how should developers spend learning time
is it worth learning new javascript frameworks
takeaways: Frameworks and libraries are short-lived; fundamentals such as design patterns and design smells carry over across languages and projects.
Allocate roughly 80% of learning time to fundamentals and 20% to frameworks, libraries and tools.
The Lindy effect suggests that technologies that have survived longer are safer to invest in, so wait before learning new ones.

Evergreen books recommended by the author include The Pragmatic Programmer, Clean Code, The Clean Coder, Domain-Driven Design, Growing Object-Oriented Software Guided by Tests, and Continuous Delivery.
summary.summary: A personal essay that argues developers waste time chasing frameworks like Angular, React, and Vue. It uses an anecdote about a mentor who redirected the author from GWT and Tapestry toward fundamentals. The author recommends spending about 80% of learning time on evergreen books and one current technology, and cites the Lindy effect to justify waiting before adopting new tools. It is opinion-based rather than a technical tutorial, and it includes no code or step-by-step instructions.
